**Yes.** A human study demonstrated whole-brain quantitative metabolite mapping using 3D proton echo-planar spectroscopic imaging (EPSI) at 3 T with a short **20 ms echo time**. In 10 healthy volunteers, it generated water-referenced concentration maps in mM for **N-acetylaspartate, choline, creatine, and myo-inositol**, with B1+, B1−, and B0 corrections. The study used two acquisition orientations to characterize broad whole-brain coverage.

This establishes feasibility, though the reported demonstration was in healthy volunteers and quantified these four metabolites; it does not by itself establish performance for every metabolite or clinical population.

**Reference:** “Whole-brain quantitative mapping of metabolites using short echo three-dimensional proton MRSI.” PMID: **25431032**.

FINAL DECISION: YES
